svg.text: Dependent Socket Retargeting: Changing (a, b) Slides the Result Socket
Because Gcd(a, b) is indexed by a and b, the dashed tethers pull the result cup's socket across linear and logarithmic zones.
A. Log-Scale Inputs & Output: (a = 1071, b = 462) → gcd = 21
Both inputs and gcd = 21 lie in the right logarithmic zone (> +8);
Result g = 21 seats cleanly inside Gcd(1071, 462) socket
No common prime factors: Div(13) = {1, 13} and Div(8) = {1, 2, 4, 8}
intersect only at {1}, pulling the result socket to g = 1.
Result g = 1 seats cleanly inside Gcd(13, 8) socket
Because Div(0) = ℕ (every number divides 0), intersecting with
Div(0) leaves Div(21) unchanged; loop exits on first check.
y = 0 immediately at loop entry → br_if $exit → return 21
Result g = 21 seats cleanly inside Gcd(21, 0) socket
Both divisor sets are all of ℕ: Div(0) ∩ Div(0) = ℕ. The unique
natural g ∈ ℕ whose divisor set is all of ℕ is g = 0!
Div(0) ∩ Div(0) = ℕ = Div(0) ⟹ socket at g = 0
y = 0 immediately at loop entry → br_if $exit → return 0
Result g = 0 seats cleanly inside Gcd(0, 0) socket
